facts.claim: In PostHog's workflows product, HogFlow.schedules (HogFlowSchedule rows) can be left PAUSED when a live workflow's audience/trigger is edited (see `_pause_schedules_on_audience_change` in products/workflows/backend/api/hog_flow.py), and the schedule API has no way to set status directly (HogFlowScheduleSerializer.update only auto-resets to ACTIVE when rrule/starts_at/timezone change, and only if not already PAUSED). Any UI or logic that (re)activates a workflow and wants its schedule to actually fire must delete existing schedules via hogFlowsSchedulesList + hogFlowsSchedulesDestroy and create a fresh one with hogFlowsSchedulesCreate, rather than relying on PATCH to revive a paused schedule.
facts.evidence: "if instance.status != HogFlowSchedule.Status.PAUSED: instance.status = HogFlowSchedule.Status.ACTIVE" (hog_flow.py HogFlowScheduleSerializer.update); test_live_audience_change_pauses_schedules confirms audience edits pause schedules with next_run_at=None.

facts.claim: In the Broadcasts wizard (products/workflows/frontend/Broadcasts/broadcastWizardLogic.ts), a HogFlow of origin_product 'broadcasts' becomes read-only in the UI (BroadcastScene renders BroadcastSummary instead of BroadcastWizard) as soon as status !== 'draft'. The only way back to the editable wizard is a status PATCH to 'draft' via hogFlowsPartialUpdate(projectId, id, {status: 'draft'}) — there is no dedicated 'unschedule' endpoint; this is the same status field used for activation.
facts.evidence: BroadcastScene.tsx: "if (broadcast.status !== 'draft') { return <BroadcastSummary /> }"; broadcastWizardLogic's launchBroadcast catch block already used `hogFlowsPartialUpdate(projectId, broadcastId, { status: 'draft' })` as its rollback-on-failure path.

F1 documents a trap (schedule PAUSE/resume asymmetry) that any future schedule-related change in this area must respect. F2 documents the status-field mechanism controlling Broadcasts editability that a future agent would otherwise have to re-derive.
